previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis with hyperglycemia, abdominal pain, and purulent drainage from her GJ tube site. She was stabilized in the ICU with an insulin drip and IV fluids, resolving her DKA. During the hospitalization, the external portion of her GJ tube was found disconnected, and a fractured segment was retained in the stomach. She underwent a successful radiologically guided procedure to remove the fragment and replace the GJ tube. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with updated insulin therapy, pain medication supply for her scheduled pain clinic visit, and instructions for tube site care. Her mental health and compliance were supported throughout by her medical guardian.

Brief Hospital Course:
Assessment and Plan: This is a ___ year old female with poorly 
controlled IDDM, gastroparesis? (recent normal gastric emptying 
studies ___, chronic pancreatitis and borderline personality 
disorder with multiple hospitalizations for abdominal pain who 
presents today with hypoerglycemia and mild anion gap metabolic 
acidosis concerning for DKA
.
# Hyperglycemia: Patient has a history of poorly controlled DM, 
she has had poor oral intake and has not been taking her insulin 
as directed. She presented with mild anion gap metabolic 
acidosis with no ketones in the urine. Her mental status was 
stable. Infectious etiologies which ___ precipitate 
hyperglycemia seemed unlikely since patient is afebrile and with 
normal CBC. Her abdominal pain/nausea/vomiting ___ be secondary 
to her chroinc gastroparesis or chronic pancreatitis. Her anion 
gap improved during hospitalization with IV fluids and agressive 
insulin regiment as per ___ diabetes team. 
.
# Port Dysfunction: While in the hospital, the patient noted 
discomfort when using the port. We discovered that the port had 
kinked and sent her to the OR for port removal and replacement 
with a double lumen port. She tolerated the procedure and 
recovery well. 
.
# Borderline personality disorder: She has medical guardian and 
cannot refuse fingersticks, insulin, etc. She initially was 
refusing blood draws, but we were able to get labs with some 
negotiation. 
.  
# Pain control: Patient has a care contract, she was given IV 
dilaudid, valium, zofran and benadryl in the ED against her 
healthcare plan. On the floor she was given all pain meds either 
PO or through her NG since there was no wittnessed vomiting. She 
tolerated these well. She is due for a narcotics renewal on 
___ and will therefore not be discharged on a new 
perscription. 
.
#  Asthma: Continued home medications, while patient was 
complaining of SOB, her respiratory rate was normal and she had 
normal O2 saturation. 
.
# PUD: Continued omeprazole as per outpatient medications. Her 
abdominal pain on presentation was not positional and not 
related to oral intake so was unlikely to represent PUD. 
.
# Urinary retention: No active problems, normal urination 
without hesitence, urgency or frequency. 
.  
# FEN: Replete electrolytes, diabetic diet  
.  
# Prophylaxis: Subcutaneous heparin, PPI, bowel regimen

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman who presented with DKA, please perform focused
oblique x-ray to evaluate for any obstruction of port.

COMPARISONS:  Portable AP radiograph from ___.

FINDINGS:  Oblique views demonstrate a right chest port catheter with no
detectable abnormality at the point of connection of the catheter with the
port.  There is possibly a kink between the clavicle and the first rib.  The
tip terminates in the mid SVC.  There is no focal consolidation, pleural
effusion or pneumothorax.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No abnormal connection of catheter with port.  Possible kink in
the mid-portion of the catheter.

PORT CHECK FROM ___

HISTORY:  ___ woman with diabetes/hx DKA and difficulties with venous
blood draws, who had a port placed at outside institution.  Patient is now
complaining of severe pain around the port with flushes and infusions.  Plain
films show question of pinch-off syndrome.

OPERATOR:  Dr. ___.

ANESTHESIA:  None.

TECHNIQUE:  Prior to the study, the procedure and alternatives and risks were
discussed with the patient by ___, PA, and consent was signed.  In
interventional radiology, the patient was placed supine on the table, and a
preprocedure huddle and timeout were performed per ___ protocol.  A scout
image was obtained over the right side of the chest and abdomen.  The port,
which had been previously accessed by ___, RN, was hooked to a
sterile contrast syringe, aspiration was performed and then injections were
performed with storage of fluoroscopy images, still images and two DSA runs,
all with hand injection.  Based on the results of this, the port was flushed
with 6 cc of sterile saline.

FINDINGS:  Scout image shows apparent looping of the proximal tubing of the
port which appears to be related to the overlying soft tissues.  The tip of
the tubing ends at the level of the proximal right atrium.  Injected contrast
exits briskly at the distal end and no leak is seen via the more proximal
portion of the tubing or around the port.  The port reservoir is seen to fill
in its entirety.  There is evidence of a short segment of fibrin sheath with
backflow of contrast along the distal 1 cm of tubing, but this does not extend
up any more proximally or inhibit brisk forward flow of contrast.  Blood was
easily obtained upon aspiration.  Note that the patient described severe pain
with each port injection including moderate pain with the flush at the end.
Contrast is seen in G-tube retention balloon.

CONCLUSION:  Portogram showing no leak or obstruction.  Short segment of
fibrin sheath is not inhibiting forward flow of contrast.  Based on the
results of plain upright chest radiograph showing possible pinch-off and the
patient's symptoms, the patient may return for port removal and replacement.

PROCEDURES:
1.  Placement of a double-lumen chest port via the left internal jugular vein.
2.  Removal of existing right subclavian chest port.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ woman with kinked existing right-sided chest
port and pain with existing port injection.  Flow study performed on ___
demonstrated no extravasation from existing port; however, the patient had
significant pain with injection and flushing.

Informed consent for both procedures was obtained after risks, benefits, and
potential complications had been discussed.  The patient was placed on the
angiographic table in supine position.  The skin of bilateral anterior chest
wall and of the left anterior neck was prepped and draped in a sterile
fashion.  Timeout protocol was carried out prior to the procedure according to
the ___ policy.

ANESTHESIA:  General endotracheal.

LOCAL ANESTHESIA:  20 mL of 1% lidocaine without and with epinephrine.

Under real-time ultrasound guidance, the left internal jugular vein was
punctured using 21-gauge micropuncture needle.  Over a 0.018 guidewire,
micropuncture needle was exchanged for a 4 ___ micropuncture sheath
followed by advancement of 0.035 ___ guidewire into the inferior vena cava.
The right port was then removed as described below.  Attention was then
diverted to the left anterior chest wall.  A linear incision was made,
inferolateral to the left internal jugular venipuncture.  After generous
infiltration of the subcutaneous tissues of the chest wall by 1% lidocaine,
using blunt dissection technique, a soft tissue pocket was created caudad to
the chest wall incision.  A double-lumen chest port was assembled and flushed
and tested for integrity.  The port was implanted into the pocket and secured
to the chest wall using 0 Prolene sutures.  Associated soft tissue tunnel was
created between the chest wall incision and left internal jugular
venipuncture.  A double-lumen permanent catheter was pulled through the
tunnel.  After appropriate dilatation of the needle tract, the permanent
catheter was advanced into the right atrium through the appropriate peel-away
sheath which was subsequently removed.  Chest wall incision was closed in
layers using 2 and 4 Vicryl suture.  Left internal jugular venipuncture was
closed using 4 Vicryl suture.  Both lumens of the port were accessed using
___ needles.  Chest port was covered with sterile dressing.

RIGHT-SIDED CHEST PORT REMOVAL:  This removal was performed after placement of
___ wire from left IJ. After generous infiltration of the subcutaneous soft
tissues overlying the existing right subclavian chest port by 1% lidocaine
with epinephrine, a linear incision was made overlying the chest port.  The
port was dissected from the chest wall and freed of the fibrous capsule. 
Permanent catheter was pulled from the right subclavian vein.  Chest wall
incision was closed in layers and covered with sterile dressing.

Dr. ___, the attending physician, supervised the procedure.

CONCLUSION:

1.  Uncomplicated placement of the double-lumen chest port into the right
atrium via the left internal jugular vein.

2.  Both chambers of the port are accessed and ready to use.

3.  Uncomplicated removal of the right chest port.
